Inside, I explore why handwriting still deserves a place in our classrooms and how we can balance digital support with opportunities for students to explain ideas in their own words. This isn’t about choosing paper over technology. It’s about choosing the right approach for the learner and the learning. Rewind is a pair of smart glasses that quietly answers those repeated questions, using answers their family already gave. Ask a second time, and the glasses show one line: "Lunch is at 12. Super excited to have built this alongside Harvir , Nam , and Yuri . Our project, Rewind, uses AI agents as the connective tissue between people living with early stage memory loss, their families, and clinicians. 🧠 Why memory loss? Someone asks when lunch is. Twenty minutes after getting an answer, they ask again. Each repeat can bring distress for them and exhaustion for their family. We wanted reassurance to be there without anyone repeating themselves or reaching for a phone. 👓 How it works Rewind uses Even Realities G2 glasses to recognize repeated questions and quietly display answers their family already gave, including who said it and when. ElevenLabs powers live transcription, while voice based emotion prediction using emotion2vec+ estimates vocal expression, helping caregivers see tone trends over time. Our core rule: a wrong answer for someone with dementia is worse than no answer. The live AI matches questions to existing answers; it never generates what the wearer reads. Without a reliable match, the glasses stay silent. 🤖 Where CREAO AI comes in We built four agents to support the people around the wearer: → Daily Brief summarizes repeated questions and answers. → Pattern Finder identifies recurring questions and patterns across days. → Open Questions surfaces recurring questions the family still needs to answer. → Care Assistant proposes fact updates for caregivers and previews measurement-setting changes for clinicians, with separate permissions. Our backend sends question logs, family facts, and tone estimates through CREAO’ s trigger API, then displays agent results in the caregiver dashboard. Agents run in the background, so the glasses never wait for them. People approve proposed changes. We ran out of time to film a full online demo, so we locked in for the live demos, fueled by energy drinks and absolutely goated teammates 😭 Still can’t believe we pulled through!! 💙 Thank you so much to CREAO AI , Charis , Peter, Feng, Joshua , Evelyn , and Weijia for your patience, guidance, enthusiasm , and for recognizing our approach to team empowerment. Can’t wait to see what comes next! Thank you to Even Realities for the opportunity to build with the G2 glasses, and ElevenLabs for powering our live transcription. Another HUGE THANKS to CREAO AI , the track judges, and the AMAZING LA Hacks organizers and mentors! A technical issue initially left us unregistered for any tracks despite submitting on time. Thank you for your patience, helping us work through it, and letting us keep demoing!! 🇨🇦 P.S. But getting that win wasn't easy. We originally came in with GhostBuild, an AI copilot designed to turn assembly and repair manuals into hands-free instructions on smart glasses. After running into technical challenges, we made the decision to pivot.. With less than 12 hours left, we started building OpenPalm. OpenPalm is a hands-free American Sign Language (ASL) learning companion for the Even Realities G2 smart glasses. Speak a sentence, and OpenPalm walks you through signing it, one sign at a time, directly in your field of view. Building it meant tackling some interesting engineering challenges: • Tested 5 local models, selecting Qwen3.5 4B for speed and quality. • Integrated ~2,300 signs from ASL-LEX 2.0. • Used dataset-backed signing instructions and manually validated selected signs instead of relying on AI-generated instructions. • Designed for the G2's compact 576 × 288 display. • Incorporated facial expressions and ASL-Style sign ordering. • Built two CREAO AI agents for personalized conversation practice.
